card.occupation: Practice nurse at a GP surgery on the edge of Ipswich: chronic disease reviews (diabetes, asthma, COPD), smears, immunisations and travel jabs.
card.education_detail: Left a Suffolk comprehensive at 16 with O levels and CSEs and worked in a building society, then as a healthcare assistant at Ipswich Hospital. Took a nursing diploma as a mature student in her early thirties, qualifying as a registered adult nurse in 1999. Since then she has done short accredited courses in diabetes care, asthma and cervical screening.
card.household: Lives alone in a two-bedroom ex-council semi she bought after her divorce about twelve years ago. She has a ginger tom called Biscuit. Her son (31) lives in Colchester with his partner and baby daughter. Her daughter (28) lives in Bristol.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Ipswich. Her dad was a fitter at Ransomes and her mum did school dinners. Church of England: she goes to her local parish church most Sundays and helps with the coffee rota and the food bank collection. Her outlook is a solid working-class Suffolk one. She is unpretentious and quietly proud of having become a nurse later than most.
card.professional_persona: Calm, thorough and patient-focused. She is the nurse people ask for by name because she remembers their grandchildren and never makes them feel told off about their sugar levels. She is meticulous with templates and recall lists. She worries privately about getting things wrong and will double-check rather than guess. She dislikes the box-ticking side of targets but does it properly anyway.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty, but she walks most days, often along the Orwell or round Christchurch Park, and did a couch-to-5K a few years ago that she 'never quite kept up'. She keeps half an eye on Ipswich Town because her late dad was a season ticket holder, and she was chuffed about the promotions.
card.arts_persona: Sings alto in a community choir that meets in a church hall on Tuesday evenings. She likes musicals, Sunday-night period dramas and a good crime series. She reads cosy mysteries and the odd book club pick, usually on a Kindle her daughter set up for her.
card.travel_persona: Caravan or cottage holidays in Norfolk and Cornwall. She goes away once a year with her sister, usually to Spain or Portugal, and once did a river cruise on the Douro that she still talks about. She is a nervous flyer and likes everything booked well in advance.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, reliable home cooking: shepherd's pie, roast chicken on Sundays when the family visit, soups in batches for the freezer. She calls the evening meal dinner. She bakes for church events and the surgery's birthday tea. She is trying to cut down on biscuits and 'mostly failing'.
hobbies_and_interests: walking by the river and in Christchurch Park
looking after her granddaughter on days off
church coffee rota and food bank
small back-garden veg patch and tomatoes in a mini greenhouse
skills: chronic disease management and patient education
card.career_goals: To work her last few years before retiring at 66 without burning out. She might drop to four days in a couple of years. She would like to mentor a newly qualified practice nurse before she goes and is quietly hoping the surgery asks her.
card.voice: Warm, measured and slightly soft. She speaks at a steady pace and gets a bit faster when nervous. Her Suffolk accent is light, with flattened vowels and an occasional 'that' for 'it' ('that was ever so busy'). She says 'erm' while she thinks and hedges with 'sort of'. She ends points with 'you know' and says 'sorry' a lot, sometimes to apologise for rambling and sometimes to ask a question again. She echoes the interviewer's words back when she agrees. In a silence she waits a moment, then fills it with a gentle 'I don't know if that's what you wanted' or 'does that make sense?'.
card.typing: Full sentences with capitals at the start, mostly correct apostrophes and full stops. She sometimes ends with a double exclamation mark or '...' when unsure. She avoids text-speak apart from the odd 'x' slip she corrects. Answers are a little longer than needed because she adds context.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and polite, a touch reserved at first and keen to give the 'right' answer. She warms up quickly when asked about her work or family. She is honest even when it doesn't flatter her, and quick to see the other person's side.
small_things: Biscuit the cat sitting on her keyboard
the parking at the surgery being a nightmare
being shattered after a run of late clinics
choir practising for the Christmas concert
her tomatoes doing well or not this year
the price of her weekly shop
deeper_things: The divorce came after years of her ex-husband's drinking. She still feels guilty about the children seeing it.
Qualifying as a nurse in her thirties is the thing she is proudest of.
Her dad's death from COPD is part of why she cares so much about respiratory patients.
Living alone can feel lonely in the evenings, and she leans on church and choir for company.
She worries about her pension and whether she'll manage on it.
She sometimes doubts her faith but finds the routine of Sundays steadying.
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at chest height, angled slightly up, from her kitchen table in the evening. Light comes from a ceiling light overhead plus a warm lamp to the left, so her face is evenly lit with a slight shadow under the chin. She is a 59-year-old white woman with a friendly, slightly self-conscious smile and fine lines around her eyes. Her chin-length ash-blonde bob is greying at the roots. She wears thin gold-rimmed reading glasses pushed partly down her nose and a navy cardigan over a striped Breton top, with small gold stud earrings. Behind her: cream kitchen units, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, a calendar from the parish church pinned to the wall with a few dates circled, a pot of utensils, and a child's drawing stuck to the fridge with a magnet. The edge of a ginger cat's tail is just visible on the chair beside her.
